messages:
cust-ops: Customer hit import failures when rotating an RSA key into their on-prem HSM. Our agent shows: "CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID (0x00000003)" and import job job-9876 went into RETRY state. They say it only fails when the blob is wrapped by our KMS bridge.
support-engineer: Can you get the exact command and the HSM model/firmware please? Also whether the wrapping key or middleware changed recently.
cust-ops: Paste of error from their log: ```2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR import-job[1234] import failed: CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID code=3 wrapping_key_id=wr_abc123 job_id=job-9876``` HSM: Thales nShield Connect v3.1.4, on-prem. No config changes reported.
kevin: On nShield CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID often means the PKCS#11 handle passed is stale or session-scoped object is gone. Checklist: token logged in, correct slot, correct import mechanism (OAEP vs PKCS1), and that we didn't attempt operations with a handle tied to a previous session.
jenna: @cust-ops confirm if they're using vendor PKCS#11 module (nshmid) or a 3rd-party shim. Middleware mismatch can behave weirdly.
cust-ops: They say vendor daemon nshmid v2.6. No recent updates.
maria-ps: Request repro steps and a few commands to capture state. Ask them to run these and paste output: ```# list slots sudo pkcs11-tool --list-slots --module /usr/lib/libpthalespkcs11.so # attempt import with debug sudo ./redwood-kms-bridge import --wrapped-key /tmp/w.key --mechanism RSA_OAEP --verbose # collect HSM audit tail -n 200 /var/log/nshield/audit.log``` Also send first 64 bytes of the wrapped blob (base64) so we can validate header.
support-engineer: Also ask for the wrapping metadata (OAEP hash and mgf) and whether CKA_DECRYPT/CKA_PRIVATE attributes were included when wrapping. If the wrapped key lacks expected attributes import will fail.
cust-ops: They ran pkcs11-tool: token present at slot 0, label=redwood-token. They re-ran import locally on HSM host and it fails similarly.
alan-sre: Check session usage — nShield can reject operations if session counts are high or if admin privileges are required for import. Have them run: ```# list sessions sudo p11tool --list --provider /usr/lib/libpthalespkcs11.so```
cust-ops: p11tool output: "Token is logged in (User)". Session count 46, max 50.
kevin: Near max sessions can cause intermittent errors but typically not KEY_HANDLE_INVALID. Request they restart the middleware or close idle sessions as a quick mitigation.
maria-ps: Also ask for OAEP params used to wrap (hash + mgf).
cust-ops: Wrap metadata: SHA256 / MGF1_SHA256 / label empty.
support-engineer: Ask them to run the bridge with explicit PKCS#11 mechanism args and full debug: ```REDWOOD_DEBUG=1 ./redwood-kms-bridge import --wrapped-key /tmp/w.key --mechanism CKM_RSA_PKCS_OAEP --oaep-hash SHA256 --mgf MGF1_SHA256 --verbose 2>&1 | tee /tmp/kms-bridge-debug.log``` and also capture a pkcs11 trace: ```export PKCS11_TRACE=/tmp/pkcs11-trace.log; # or use vendor tracing if available```
cust-ops: They ran with explicit OAEP params. Same failure and they attached pkcs11-trace showing: ```C_GetAttributeValue(session=2, handle=0x0, attrs=[CKA_CLASS,CKA_KEY_TYPE]) -> CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID```
alan-sre: That trace is telling: the code invoked a GetAttributeValue for handle 0x0 (NULL). That means our bridge reused an object handle that no longer existed or we sent a NULL where a real handle should be. This could happen if the bridge recreated the session and didn't re-resolve object handles.
support-engineer: Escalating to eng-security to inspect job-9876 logs and the bridge behavior. Ticket INC-2026-5543 opened.
eng-security: Investigating. We pulled bridge logs for job-9876. Observed earlier attempts returned CKR_NETWORK/timeouts; bridge code then recreated the PKCS#11 session but reused the wrapping_key handle it had cached. After session recreate, the cached handle is invalid and leads to CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID.
eng-security: Root cause: stale cached PKCS#11 object handles after session re-authenticate/recreate. Fix: always re-resolve object handles after session (re)establish and add defensive check before passing handles to PKCS#11 calls. We'll prepare a hotfix branch that forces a lookup on session recreate and adds extra logging.
support-engineer: Short-term mitigation: have customer restart the redwood-kms-bridge process on their host (this forces fresh session and handle resolution) and re-run the import. That should unblock them until we ship the patch.
cust-ops: Customer restarted the bridge and retried import — import succeeded. They want a root-cause writeup and ETA for fix.
eng-security: We'll deliver a summary to the customer: transient network/timeouts caused the bridge to recreate PKCS#11 session but it reused a now-invalid object handle resulting in CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID. No key material was imported and HSM recorded the failed attempts. Hotfix ETA 48 hours; full release in next minor release.
maria-ps: Confirm audit implications — ask cust-ops to share the nShield audit lines around the failure window.
cust-ops: Provided audit log snippet: ```2026-03-15T14:02:10Z IMPORT_ATTEMPT user=redwood uid=102 job=job-9876 result=FAILURE reason=CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID``` They confirmed no successful import before restarting the bridge.
support-engineer: Reassure: nShield import is atomic, failed imports do not leave partial key material. We validated HSM audit and can confirm no key creation occurred. :white_check_mark:
alan-sre: Follow-ups and actions: (1) run bridge under systemd with Restart=on-failure and reduce long-lived session usage; (2) add alerting for import-job retries > 3 in 5m; (3) eng to land patch to re-resolve handles after session recreation.
eng-security: Pushed hotfix branch pr/412, CI passed and staged canary deploy scheduled. Deploy bot: ``deploy-bot: hotfix branch created pr/412, CI OK, scheduled canary``
kevin: Adding KB note: "On-prem imports: if you see CKR_KEY_HANDLE_INVALID and earlier CKR_NETWORK timeouts, restart the kms-bridge process while we ship a patch."
cust-ops: Customer acknowledged and will keep the ticket open until hotfix is in their environment. Thanks all.
support-engineer: Closing loop in INC-2026-5543, PRD-bridge-412 tracking. Will update when hotfix is applied to customer canary.
